configuration: U-570 as captured, August–September 1941; British hull survey datums with German 1941 fittings; raised attack periscope
acquisition: September 6 schematics/photographs downloaded over certificate-verified HTTPS; acquisition.json records URLs and SHA-256. Older September 5 files used the documented host-scoped certificate fallback. No third-party game geometry or textures used.

sources.title: ONI report on U-570, inspected September 23–26, 1941
supports: Four bow tubes and one stern tube, 14 torpedoes in the surveyed load
Diesels, electric motors, saddle tanks, deck fittings and compartment order
8.8 cm deck gun and 20 mm platform weapon
Approximately 8 kn maximum submerged speed in the captured-boat survey; the 7.6 kn nominal game setting is not a reproduction of this trial
Explicitly says net cutters depicted on enclosed plans were NOT fitted to captured U-570.
sources.limits: Survey dimensions and load are not a complete build specification; not every feature was directly measured.

sources.title: General arrangement enclosure A to the ONI report
supports: Qualitative profile, plan, tower and internal machinery order
sources.limits: Older lower-resolution copy. Fidelity pass uses separately registered high-resolution U.S. Navy redraw; both preserved.

sources.title: Photographs accompanying the U-570 survey
supports: Narrow slotted wood deck, central rails, open bridge, tower fittings and deck gun
Bridge wood lining, voicepipes, compass repeaters; forward/aft deck loading hatches and stowage covers
sources.limits: Perspective inspection only; no unverified dimensional extraction.

sources.title: Type VIIC characteristics, uboat.net
supports: 67.1 m overall length, 6.2 m beam, 4.74 m draft, 769 tonne surfaced displacement, 17.7 knot surface speed
sources.limits: Nominal class envelope, not the measured loading state of the retained U-570 images.

sources.title: G7a torpedo operating modes
supports: 44 knot / 5000 m fast setting, 533 mm diameter and approximately 7.16 m length
sources.limits: Single selected game run mode; period reliability, gyro turn, speed settings, depth errors and detonator mechanisms are not recreated.

sources.title: C.B.4318: British technical report on ex-U-570 / HMS Graph (1943)
sources.kind: Primary captured-boat technical survey; original HTML retained
supports: Main ballast blown with compressed air during recovery
Diesel/electric propulsion and approximately 8 kn submerged speed
sources.limits: Later British fittings are not backdated to 1941. Survey beam/draft differ from rounded nominal class dimensions. Load-dependent displacement is not equated with existing gameplay mass. Report notes an erroneous No.3 ballast-tank volume; no uncritical use of that figure.

sources.title: U.S. Navy David Taylor Model Basin redraw/translation of captured U-570 general arrangement
supports: Longitudinal gun, tower, periscope, deck and stern appendage positions
Six pressure-body sections showing circular bilges, saddle lobes, casing and keel
Early single AA basket and external torpedo stowage
sources.limits: Class drawing is not an unqualified as-captured inventory: net cutters shown but absent by ONI report. Midpoint/waterline registration interpreted; local scan/drawing disagreement ±0.15–0.3 m. Six sections do not supply a complete yard table of offsets. Raised scope extension differs between views.
sources.rights: U.S. government archival redraw; reference-only reproduction, credited to U.S. Navy / David Taylor Model Basin and U-boat Archive.

sources.title: British docking plan 1732Z/12, Plate 4, ex-U-570 as fitted
supports: 220 ft 1¾ in overall = 67.10045 m; 20 ft 2¼ in beam = 6.15315 m
15 ft 7½ in surfaced draft = 4.7625 m
19 ft 7½ in keel to casing deck = 5.9817 m; 2 ft 5 in casing above pressure crown
15 ft 6 in pressure diameter = 4.7244 m; bridge lip 11 ft 1¼ in above casing
Screw lateral centres ±3 ft 8 in; rudder stock lateral centres ±2 ft ½ in; stern profiles
sources.limits: Dimensioned drawing preferred to nominal rounded class dimensions. Derived heights use one selected surfaced datum. Loading changes draft. Exact scan outlines/appendage longitudinal centres remain interpreted; German gun fittings come from 1941 sources. Propeller diameter lettering is not confidently resolved; 1940 class manual supplies 1.620 m provisional diameter.
sources.rights: British government wartime archival engineering drawing; Crown copyright term expired; archive credited. Modern archive text is not used as artwork.

sources.title: British U-570 interrogation, VI: Details of U-570, captured notebook characteristics
sources.kind: Contemporary primary interrogation / captured notebook transcription
supports: 67.10 m overall, 65.90 m waterline, 4.70 m pressure diameter, 49.40 m pressure length
Maximum raised periscope 14.612 m above keel
sources.limits: Metric class/notebook values and British measured imperial survey differ slightly. 14.612 m is a maximum extension, not the scope height in every photo. Reported loading/displacement is not assumed equal to gameplay state.

sources.title: Type VIIC preliminary information, effective 15 July 1940, propellers
sources.kind: Primary official class manual, archival translated transcription
supports: Three blades, 1620 mm diameter, 1540 mm pitch; ahead rotation tops outward
sources.limits: Class specification, not a legible measured U-570 blade drawing. Actual blade outline, thickness, skew and handed visual reconstruction remain estimates.

sources.title: Captured main-ballast arrangement (Plate 27) and British watertight-compartment plan 1732Z/13
supports: Six major interior spaces, central ballast and outboard saddle/fuel-ballast arrangement
sources.limits: External free-flooding volume and pressure spaces are visually distinguished but still share one game collision envelope. Conservative disjoint room cells are not a calibrated tank capacity/trim model.
